summary: The set printer is fine, but `_print_dict` sorts `expr.items()` directly, which compares SymPy objects and raises TypeError (`cannot determine truth value of Relational`) for any dict with 2+ symbolic keys — a crash and regression versus the previous no-crash behavior. The fix only works for single-key dicts (as in the repro), so it is incomplete and fragile.

issues.description: `sorted(expr.items())` compares SymPy Expr keys via `<`, which returns a Relational whose bool() raises TypeError. Any dict with 2+ non-trivially-comparable keys (e.g. Symbol keys) makes srepr crash. Should sort by a key function (e.g. default_sort_key / str) or not sort at all.
Regression: previously `srepr({x: y, a: b})` returned a string without error; now it raises TypeError. Behavior for multi-key dicts is worse than before the patch.
Fix only demonstrably works for the single-element dict in the issue; multi-element dicts (the general case) are unresolved/broken, so the issue is not fully fixed.

Sorting set on printed strings gives determinism but is inconsistent with list/tuple printers which preserve order; sorting choice for repr should follow sympy conventions (default_sort_key) rather than lexical string sort.
